title: Understanding AI Stakes to Break Production Code: Philip Rathle
talk_summary: This is a facilitated round-table (Philip Rathle of Neo4j) where practitioners share production-AI lessons organized around 'stakes' (low vs high, pilot vs co-pilot vs human-in-loop). There is no system architecture to copy, but several concrete, mechanism-level practices emerge: use the LLM to write deterministic code instead of reasoning directly, start evals on day zero, avoid premature model downsizing, and expose AI uncertainty to users.

takeaways.technique: LLM writes code instead of answering directly
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than asking the model to solve a reasoning problem (e.g. find the outlier in a spreadsheet), ask it to emit code that solves the problem, then run that code deterministically with the LLM out of the loop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of asking the llm to solve a problem ... just ask it to write the code to solve that problem ... then you can leave the llm out of the loop

takeaways.what_they_do: Build the eval harness and the data it needs at the same time as the app, so you can tell whether a prompt/fine-tune change is better or worse before shipping.

takeaways.technique: Validate with big model first, downsize later
takeaways.what_they_do: Prove the task is possible with the strongest model, then treat smaller/fine-tuned models as an optimization; starting small often wrongly concludes the task is impossible.
takeaways.evidence_quote: moving down the model size stack or fine-tuning as optimizations and you want to validate the product need and whether it works ... usually with a better model first

takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly size how fast and how accurate the task actually needs to be before picking a model, because 'best and fastest' can burn a year's budget in a day.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're burning a Year's budget within a day which is very possible with this stuff then maybe you need smaller models

takeaways.technique: Kill more projects than you experiment on
takeaways.what_they_do: Focus experimentation on the few projects that can actually reach production accuracy expectations; abandon the rest early rather than spreading effort.
takeaways.evidence_quote: kill more projects than experimentation ... a lot of these experimentation even with the best effort will never meet the user expectation on accuracy

takeaways.technique: Expose AI uncertainty in the UI
takeaways.what_they_do: Don't hide that output is AI-generated: stream slowly, use distinct colors/icons, and give users source/citation views so they validate rather than trust blindly.
